title: A weekly day of quiet
hookLine: a half-day of mindfulness each week
tomorrow: Mai is broke all summer. can her weekly gift be time?

cards: Sunday is the program's one day off. Jess, Mai's roommate, wants the art museum downtown, all day. Mai had pictured a quiet morning: no phone, no studio, no talking.
Can a day be both? Inside Buddhism there are two honest answers to what a quiet day is, and each has good teachers behind it.

teach.b: The first view: quiet means apart. The suttas show the Buddha himself stepping away.
In one, he tells the monks he wants to go into seclusion for three months, and no one should come to him except the one who brings his alms food.

Afterward he says: if anyone asks, tell them the Teacher spent the rains in mindfulness of breathing. The Pali word is viveka, seclusion. Its best case: you can't hear your own mind while the world keeps talking.
A quiet day needs real edges: phone off, no plans, sitting and walking. The second view: quiet means slow, inside ordinary life.

The Vietnamese teacher Thich Nhat Hanh taught a weekly day of mindfulness in which the chores still get done, washing dishes, sweeping, making tea, only slowly, each one done for itself and not to be finished with.

Its best case: a quiet that exists only away from life won't survive Monday, so you practice where you live. Both views share the heart of it: some part of every week, set apart, so the mind can settle.

teach.h: EDGES AROUND IT, OR INSIDE IT.
teach.b: They differ on where the edges go: around the day, or inside it.
Mai's Sunday could hold both, a quiet morning with real edges, then an afternoon in the museum, looking at one painting long enough to see it. A quiet day isn't empty. It's unhurried.

how: Buddhists keep weekly quiet time in different ways: some set aside a half-day or day of silence, sitting and walking with phones off; communities in Thich Nhat Hanh's tradition keep a day of mindfulness with sitting, walking and chores done slowly.

games.q: what does “a weekly day of quiet” mean?
o: a weekly fast from food, kept from dawn to dark
a day off spent catching up on sleep and errands
a regular stretch of the week kept unhurried and apart

games.q: two views of a quiet day — tap the pairs.

s: once he was teaching, the Buddha never took time alone
in one sutta he goes into seclusion for three months, seeing only the one who brought his food.
a quiet day in Buddhism has to mean doing nothing at all
one view keeps the chores and does them slowly; quiet is unhurried, not empty.
the Pali word viveka means seclusion, being set apart
the first view's word: real edges around the quiet.

games.q: a friend says a 'quiet day' with chores and errands in it is just a normal day with a nicer name. give the best case for the other side.
o: done slowly, each chore can be the practice, and that quiet survives into Monday
chores go faster when you're calm, so the rest of the day is free for fun
he's right; only a full retreat in the woods ever counts as quiet
games.why: Thich Nhat Hanh's weekly day of mindfulness keeps the chores and slows them down. the other view sets real edges, as the Buddha did when he withdrew to sit alone.

practice: Stand and walk very slowly across the room and back, as if this minute belonged to a quiet day. Feel each foot lift, move and land. Then sit for the rest of the time, and notice that the quiet came with you.

wordCard.voice: A weekly day of quiet: part of every week set apart, with edges around it or slowness inside it.

orig.note: Pali: seclusion, being set apart, of body and of mind.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: a quiet day, unhurried rather than empty, once every week. Sunday, kept.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 54.11 (Icchanangala): three months of seclusion; the rains spent in mindfulness of breathing
